notes: Accepts exact Vulkan0, Vulkan1, Vulkan0,Vulkan1, and Vulkan1,Vulkan0. Empty tokens, duplicates, unknown names, and more than two names return before any device lookup, so nothing falls back to the first GPU.

Single selection uses LLAMA_SPLIT_MODE_NONE and a llama_max_devices tensor_split of 1 followed by zeros. A pair uses LLAMA_SPLIT_MODE_LAYER and 1,1 then zeros. The same vectors are what requested.tensor_split reports. Device pointers stay alive until the model and context are freed.

device_population is the selected device count, 1 or 2. device_registry_count is ggml_backend_dev_count and includes the CPU registration. vendor_population is SINGLE_VENDOR or MIXED_VENDOR from the selected description properties. A single device is never labeled mixed.

Pair workload text remains DEVICES=Vulkan0,Vulkan1 or DEVICES=Vulkan1,Vulkan0 with no extra comma. A single device hash uses only that name. Requested 128, actual 256, batch, ubatch, quant, tokens, atol 0.01, and rtol 0.01 are unchanged.

CPU loading stays on the CPU device with n_gpu_layers 0 and both offload flags false. GPU loading still requests INT_MAX layers. This patch does not claim those layers stayed on the selected GPU; per-layer ownership still requires llama logs. AMD device_id stays UNKNOWN when props.device_id is null, and capacity_qualified stays false.
The same parse, JSON-array, tensor-split, vendor-label, and name-join helpers are executed from qual_self_test. Comparator, corruption, padding, and SHA-256 abc checks are unchanged.
